profile.name: Brooke Winkler
profile.degreeLine: B.S. Mechanical Engineering & Aerospace Engineering · Honors Program · Michigan Technological University · Expected April 2030
profile.target: Seeking a Summer 2027 motorsports engineering internship
profile.objective: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering student at Michigan Technological University (Honors Program, Class of 2030) with four years of FIRST Robotics design, fabrication, electrical, and leadership experience, including a FIRST Impact Award and World Championship qualification. Independent research into the 2026 Formula 1 power unit regulations and their effect on racing.

experience.role: Captain — Design, Strategy, Build & Electrical Lead
bullets: Led mechanical design, fabrication, electrical systems, and competition strategy for a student-run FIRST Robotics Competition team.
Served as the primary contributor for mechanical and electrical development during senior year, taking designs from CAD through fabrication, assembly, wiring, and competition use.
Utilized SolidWorks for detailed mechanical design and 3D printing, CNC machining, and laser cutting for rapid prototyping and final components.
Supported robot programming and controls development using Java and WPILib while independently tuning robot parameters and operational values.
Led and mentored newer team members in mechanical design, fabrication, electrical work, strategy, and competition operations.
Guided the team through regional and state-level competition and qualification for the FIRST World Championship.
Supported media operations for the Red Bull Racing Detroit Showrun, gaining firsthand exposure to professional motorsports media and event operations.
Served as a photographer and journalist, sharing experiences with local news outlets to promote events.
Conduct client outreach through cold calling and email to develop business opportunities for a student-run web development company.
Conduct market research to identify potential clients and evaluate local business needs and opportunities.
Support marketing and communications efforts while collaborating with developers on client-facing initiatives.

analysis.role: 2026 Formula 1 Power Unit Regulations — Independent Research
bullets: Conducting research into the 2026 Formula 1 power unit regulations and their effects on racing.
Investigating changes in powertrain design, hybridization, vehicle performance, and competitive racing dynamics.
Served as varsity team captain during senior year after three years as a varsity athlete.
Earned All-Catholic, All-League, and All-Academic honors.
Led backstage technical operations and crews across multiple productions, coordinating scene changes, props, logistics, and crew responsibilities during rehearsals and performances.
Developed practical solutions to complex production and time-management challenges while maintaining show readiness under high-pressure conditions.
Mentored two FIRST Tech Challenge teams, including helping establish a rookie team and supporting another team through qualification for the Michigan State Championship.
Volunteered at FIRST robotics competitions and supported students and teams throughout competition operations.

honors: 3× Top Technician in the State of Michigan
FIRST Impact Award · World Championship Qualifier
